title: Add torch.autograd.graph.node_creation_hook
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #189284

Adds a public context manager that registers a thread-local hook fired
once for every autograd Node created within it, with the freshly created
Node as argument. This gives users a creation-time dual of
saved_tensors_hooks: the hook can inspect the node, record it, stash
entries in node.metadata, or register backward pre/post hooks on it.

The motivating use case is attributing backward-pass memory allocations
to the forward region that created the graph: capture TLS state (e.g.
torch.cuda.memory._set_memory_metadata) at node creation and restore it
around the node's execution via register_prehook/register_hook. More
generally it subsumes ad-hoc seq_nr-range bookkeeping for identifying
"all nodes created in a region", and unlike that approach it composes
with create_graph double-backward and checkpoint recomputation because
the TLS rides at::ThreadLocalState onto engine worker threads.

The hook fires only after the node is fully populated -- specifically
after all tensors saved for backward have been stored on it -- so a hook
that inspects the node sees its complete saved state. Firing therefore
happens at the tail of each node-attachment path rather than from a
single funnel inside impl::set_gradient_edge, which runs before saved
tensors are attached.

Design notes, in review order:

- aten/src/ATen/NodeCreationHooks.{h,cpp}: TLS stack of SafePyObject
  hooks plus an is_firing reentrancy guard, mirroring SavedTensorHooks;
  lives in ATen so ThreadLocalState can snapshot it.
- torch/csrc/autograd/node.h, function.cpp: fire_node_creation_hooks
  fires at node-attachment time, not in the Node constructor: at
  construction no owning intrusive_ptr exists yet, so the node cannot
  be safely wrapped in a PyObject, and next_edges aren't wired. Every
  attachment path fires a node exactly once by construction, so the
  per-node fired flag is a TORCH_INTERNAL_ASSERT guarding that invariant
  rather than a runtime dedup.
- torch/csrc/autograd/variable.cpp, VariableTypeUtils.h: impl and
  utility rebase_history now return the node actually attached as the
  new history -- the CopySlices node when rebasing through a view, else
  the passed-in function -- so callers fire hooks on the composed outer
  node, never the inner one it wraps.
- tools/autograd/gen_variable_type.py: generated apply functions fire at
  the very end, after emit_save_outputs stores saved tensors. The rebase
  path captures rebase_history's return so the hook sees the CopySlices
  node; the foreach path fires once per grad_fn after the loop.
- torch/csrc/autograd/custom_function.{cpp,h}, python_function.cpp:
  _wrap_outputs threads out the attached node (cdata, or the CopySlices
  node for a dirty view input) so both C++ and Python custom Functions
  fire once after save_variables.
- torch/csrc/autograd/autograd_not_implemented_fallback.cpp: firing is
  hoisted out of the per-output loop so a grad_fn shared across multiple
  outputs fires exactly once; the view in-place branch fires its fresh
  CopySlices node inside the loop.
- Remaining manual attachment sites (VariableTypeManual copy_/_fw_primal/
  _make_dual, functions/comm.cpp Scatter/Gather, data_parallel.h,
  distributed/autograd/utils.cpp, python_torch_functions_manual.cpp) fire
  explicitly after set_history/rebase_history. The lazy AsStridedBackward0
  regeneration in VariableHooks::grad_fn and AccumulateGrad nodes created
  lazily in backward intentionally do not fire.
- torch/csrc/autograd/engine.h, python_engine.{h,cpp}: libtorch_cpu
  cannot call into Python, so firing dispatches through a new
  Engine::call_node_creation_hook virtual overridden by PythonEngine
  (same pattern as get_default_saved_variable_hooks), which takes the
  GIL and wraps the node via functionToPyObject.
- torch/autograd/graph.py, init.cpp, pyi, docs: public context manager
  and bindings modeled on saved_tensors_hooks.

Test Plan:

New tests in test/test_autograd.py cover: per-node firing with node
identity, multi-output nodes firing once, nesting (outermost first),
custom Functions, in-place ops, lazy view grad_fn regeneration, no
firing outside the context, AccumulateGrad not firing, propagation to
create_graph double-backward and checkpoint recomputation via
ThreadLocalState, hook exceptions propagating to the forward op,
reentrancy (ops inside a hook don't recurse), the backward pre/post-hook
attribution pattern, and a multi-output op through the not-implemented
fallback firing its shared grad_fn exactly once (the case the loop hoist
protects, which would trip the fired-twice assert if mis-hoisted).

```
python test/test_autograd.py -k node_creation_hook -v
python test/test_autograd.py TestAutograd
python test/test_autograd.py TestMultithreadAutograd
```

All pass (16 node_creation_hook tests). Also smoke-tested under
torch.compile: hooks fire for nodes created during Dynamo tracing plus
the final CompiledFunctionBackward, consistent with saved_tensors_hooks
behavior under compile.

Authored with Claude Code.

items.author: albanD
items.body: It should propagate to any worker thread from any systems.
items.diff_hunk:
@@ -456,6 +457,72 @@ def disable_saved_tensors_hooks(error_message: str) -> Generator[None, None, Non
             torch._C._autograd._saved_tensors_hooks_disable(maybe_prev_message)
 
 
+class node_creation_hook:
+    """Context-manager that registers a hook called on each autograd Node created within it.
+
+    In that context, ``hook`` is called once for every autograd graph node
+    created by operations on tensors that require grad, with the freshly
+    created :class:`torch.autograd.graph.Node` as its only argument. At that
+    point the node's ``next_edges`` are already set up, so the hook may
+    inspect the node, record it, stash entries in ``node.metadata``, or
+    register backward hooks on it via
+    :meth:`~torch.autograd.graph.Node.register_hook` and
+    :meth:`~torch.autograd.graph.Node.register_prehook`.
+
+    The hook should have the following signature::
+
+        hook(node: torch.autograd.graph.Node) -> None
+
+    The registration is thread-local and propagates to autograd engine worker

+class node_creation_hook:
+    """Context-manager that registers a hook called on each autograd Node created within it.
+
+    In that context, ``hook`` is called once for every autograd graph node
+    created by operations on tensors that require grad, with the freshly
+    created :class:`torch.autograd.graph.Node` as its only argument. At that
+    point the node's ``next_edges`` are already set up, so the hook may

+    :meth:`~torch.autograd.graph.Node.register_hook` and
+    :meth:`~torch.autograd.graph.Node.register_prehook`.
+
+    The hook should have the following signature::
+
+        hook(node: torch.autograd.graph.Node) -> None
+
+    The registration is thread-local and propagates to autograd engine worker
+    threads: if backward is run under this context (or graph nodes are
+    created during backward, e.g. with ``create_graph=True`` or inside
+    checkpoint recomputation), the hook also fires for those nodes.
+
+    Nodes created by hooks themselves do not trigger hooks again. When
+    nesting this context-manager, all active hooks are called for each node,
+    outermost first.
+
+    One motivating use case is attributing memory allocated during backward

items.diff_hunk:
@@ -11356,6 +11356,176 @@ def backward(ctx, grad_out):
             out = Func.apply(a)
         out.backward()
 
+    def test_node_creation_hook(self):
+        a = torch.randn(2, requires_grad=True)
+        nodes = []
+
+        b = a * 2
+        with torch.autograd.graph.node_creation_hook(nodes.append):
+            c = b.exp()
+            d = c + c
+        e = d.sum()
+
+        self.assertEqual([n.name() for n in nodes], ["ExpBackward0", "AddBackward0"])
+        self.assertIs(nodes[0], c.grad_fn)
+        self.assertIs(nodes[1], d.grad_fn)
+
+    def test_node_creation_hook_multi_output_fires_once(self):
+        nodes = []
+        a = torch.randn(5, requires_grad=True)
+        with torch.autograd.graph.node_creation_hook(nodes.append):
+            values, indices = a.sort()
+        self.assertEqual(len(nodes), 1)
+        self.assertIs(nodes[0], values.grad_fn)

items.author: ezyang
items.body:
So it would seem that Fable has optimized for minimal number of code changes necessary to get mostly constructed Nodes to the callback function, re:

> We should either say that the Node is not ready for inspection or actually trigger when ready!

Claude's general claim is that it is not easy to edit only one spot to make it work:

```
  The obvious fix — fire once at the end of the vector set_history loop (that's functions/utils.h, not
  codegen) — closes the multi-output gap for codegen ops. But set_history is not the only path into
  set_gradient_edge. Custom Functions call set_gradient_edge directly from _wrap_outputs, in-place ops go
  through rebase_history, plus CopySlices and the lazy AsStridedBackward0. The whole reason the hook lives in
  set_gradient_edge is that it's the one shared chokepoint all those paths funnel through.
```

I have to convince myself this is actually true. I now agree that this strategy here is potentially slop (though possibly useful slop?)

items.body: Human note: this PR has to studiously update EVERY cpp autograd function to call `fire_node_creation_hooks` after it's done setting grad fn on all the outputs. There isn't really any other way to guarantee the autograd node is fully formed otherwise.

items.author: ezyang
items.body: You see this in a few places, but it would seem that sometimes when we rebase or otherwise change the autograd node, we lose access to the final real autograd node (and thus cannot call the hook on it). So we end up having to pass these around. This technically results in some extra refcount bumps so it could potentially be not so good.
